title: Protocol for designing and bioprinting multi-layered constructs to reconstruct an endothelial-epithelial 3D model
protocol: Download and install TinkerCAD®.
Create a new account or log in via your preference.
Click on “Create your first 3D Design”.
Select basic shapes from the shapes menu and drag them to the table.
Choose the cylindrical form and demonstrate its use.
Select the white squares at the vertices of the cylinder to modify its length and width to 10.0 mm.
Modify the height of the cylinder by selecting the middle white square and setting it to 1 mm.
Select the object and copy-paste it.
Click on the surface of the new object, and by using the mouse’s left button, drag it to fit the first object.
Click at the dark arrow in the middle of the objects and lift one of the objects 1 mm above the other.
Select only the object below and click on export (right corner at the top of the screen).
Select the option “The selected shape” and the panel “For 3D Print”, select click on “.STL”.
Name the file as “Bottom”.
Select only the object above, repeat steps to fit and lift one object above another.
Repeat export step for the upper object and name it as “Top” file.
Close Tinkercad.
Download Prusa Slicer.
Install PrusaSlicer by double-clicking the download file.
Open PrusaSlicer and click on “Configuration Tab > Mode”.
Select “Expert” mode.
Select the “Print settings” tab on the configuration menu.
Configure “Layer height” to 0.2 mm.
Configure “First layer height” to 0.2 mm.
Configure “Vertical Shells” to 0.
Configure “Horizontal shells”, “Solid Layers”, “Top”, and “Bottom” as 0.
Select “Infill” on the left menu.
Configure “Fill density” at 50%.
Configure “Fill Pattern” as “Rectilinear”.
Configure “Combine infill every” to 1.
Configure “Solid Infill” to 0.
Configure “Fill Angle” to 90.
Select "Skirt and Brim" on the left menu.
Configure “Loops (minimum)” to 0 in the “skirt” panel.
Configure “Brim width” to 0 in the “brim” panel.
Select the “speed” option from the left menu.
Configure the speed of “infill” to 5 at the “Speed for print moves” panel.
Configure the speed of “Support material” to 5 at the “Speed for print moves” panel.
Configure the speed of “Bridges” to 5 at the “Speed for print moves” panel.
Configure “Travel” to 20 at the “Speed for non-print moves” panel.
Configure “First layer speed” to 5 at the “Modifiers” panel.
Select “Advanced” on the left menu.
Configure all variables to 0.4 at the “Extrusion width” panel.
Save the configuration by clicking on diskette.
Select “Filament settings” and “Filament” from the left menu.
Configure the “Diameter” as 12 mm on the “filament” panel.
Set the value as 0 for all options on the "Temperature" panel.
Save the configuration by clicking on diskette.
Select “Printer settings” and then select “General” on the left menu.
Click on “Set” at the “Bed Shape” option in the “Size and coordinates” panel.
Change the shape of the bed to X: “300”, Y: “300”, Origin X “100” and Origin Y “140”.
Click on “OK”.
Configure the “Max Print height” to “100” at the “Size and coordinate” panel.
Set the “Z offset” to 1.2 at the “Size and coordinate” panel.
Select “Custom G-Code” on the left menu.
Substitute the content in the “Start G-Code” panel to: “G1 X0 Y70 Z1.4 F3000”.
Substitute the content in the “End of G-code” panel to: “G1 Z25 F3000 G4 P5000 T0 G1 X0 Y70 Z1.4”.
Select "Extruder 1" on the left menu.
Set "Nozzle Diameter" as 0.4 mm at the "Size" panel.
Set the value at "0" for "Length" at the "Retraction" panel.
Set the value at "0" for "Length" at the "Retraction tool when tool is disabled" panel.
Proceed with steps 11a to 11c for "Extruder 2" on the left menu.
Set the value of "Extruder offset" at "85" for "X coordinate" at the "Position" panel.
Return to the "Platter" at the "Configuration menu".
Import the two "STL" files exported from TinkerCAD.
Click "Yes" at the "Multi-part object detect" warning message.
Click on "Bottom" on the right menu.
Move both parts simultaneously and replace them at position "(X,Y):(0,70)".
Preheat 50 mL of PBS at 50°C using a heating plate.
Cover the top of the Becker with aluminum foil paper to avoid PBS evaporation.
Let it stabilize for at least 30 min under a fume hood.
Add 5 g of gelatin from porcine skin and stir at 250 RPM until it forms a clear solution.
Add slowly (dropwise) 0.5 mL of methacrylic anhydride, MA.
Transfer 0.5 mL to a beaker and add using a plastic pipette.
Cover the solution with aluminum foil.
Let it react at 50°C for 2 h.
Monitor the temperature every 15 min to ensure it does not shift more than ± 2°C.
Hydrate dialysis membrane in deionized water, about 2 pieces of 50 cm each.
Test the membranes with deionized water for holes or leaks before use.
Preheat 50 mL of PBS.
Dilute the gelatin-MA solution.
Let it stir for 10 min at the same conditions previously described.
Pour the solution of gelatin-MA equally into dialysis membranes using a glass funnel.
Close one end of each membrane, leaving space for air to aid in floating and homogenization.
Dialyze with distilled water at 40°C for 5 days with mild agitation.
Cover the beaker with aluminum foil to prevent evaporation during dialysis.
Change the distilled water twice daily with preheated water and homogenize GelMA by flipping upside-down.
At the end of dialysis, remove the content from the membranes.
Mix the membrane contents with 100 mL of ultrapure water preheated at 40°C.
Agitate for 15 minutes using magnetic stirring.
Transfer the solution to 50 mL conical tubes and store at -80°C for at least 2 days before lyophilization.
Adjust the volume in each tube to approximately 25 mL and store them horizontally during freezing.
Retrieve flasks from -80°C, remove taps, and add tissue paper on top of each flask.
Lyophilize the reagent for 2 days.
Retrieve GelMA from -20°C.
Weigh 320 mg of prepared GelMA (8 wt.%).
Mix it with 4 ml of PBS in a 5 mL flask with a cap.
Add 20 mg of photoinitiator (0.5% m/v) to the mixture and dissolve it at 37°C for at least 4 h or overnight.
Cover the flask with aluminum foil.
Filter the solution of GelMA using a syringe and a polypropylene 0.22 μm filter under a laminar flow cabinet.
Retrieve HUVEC cells from the incubator, remove the media, and resuspend the cells using Trypsin/EDTA solution.
Incubate the cells in 1 volume of 0.25% Trypsin/EDTA warm-solution for 5 min.
Inactivate the Trypsin/EDTA solution with the same media volume 1:1 (DMEM/F12 supplemented with 10% Fetal Bovine Serum and 1% Penicillin/Streptomycin).
Retrieve filtered GelMA or GelMA/Geltrex® and transfer it to a laminar flow cabinet.
Remove the supernatant from the cells-trypsin-DMEM-12 solution using a 1000 μL pipette.
Continue removing the supernatant with a 100 μL pipette carefully to avoid aspirating the cells.
Add filtered GelMA or GelMA/Geltrex into the HUVEC cell pellet and dissociate it with slow up-down movements.
Use cell strainers if cell aggregates form during the process.
Transfer the HUVEC-bioink solution to a 5 mL sterile syringe using pipettes.
Insert the syringe plunger carefully to remove any bubbles formed inside the syringe.
Add a 22G needle without a bevel to the syringe containing the HUVEC-bioink solution.
Transfer syringes with HUVEC-bioink solution to the refrigerator for 5 min.
Transfer syringes with A549-bioink solution to the refrigerator for 5 min.
Sterilize bioprinter and mounting parts using 70% (v/v) alcohol.
Expose sterilized equipment to UV light for 15 min.
Turn on the bioprinter.
Connect the bioprinter to the computer using a USB cable.
Open Pronterface software to control the printer.
Click on the “House” box in Pronterface.
Digit "G28" in the command line of Pronterface to set zero for all coordinates.
Retrieve the syringes with cell-bioink from the refrigerator.
Insert the syringe with HUVEC cell-bioink into the left syringe holder.
Adjust the height of the needle to 1.4 mm using the command line: "G1 X0 Y70 Z1.4 F3000".
Send the command to the bioprinter.
Extrude the bioink until it starts flowing from the needle to the petri dish.
Configure the “length” as “0.1” mm for better precision during extrusion.
Lift the syringe 25 mm using the command: "G1 Z25 F3000".
Send the command to the bioprinter.
Set up the next syringe at right holder with A549-bioink.
Lift the nozzle and set the extruder 2 to the X-offset position.
Translate the X-axis to the right syringe using the command: “G1 X-85 F3000”
Activate the extruder 2 by using the command: “T1”
Move Z to touch the petri dish by using the command: “G1 Z1.4 F3000”
Lift the Extruder 2 and return to the position of step starting position (Extruder 1, HUVEC bioink) by using the following commands line
Lift the syringe 25 mm by using the command: “G1 Z25 F3000”
Translate the X′ axis to the left syringe using the command: “G1 X0 F3000”
Activate the extruder 1 using the command: “T0”
Move Z to touch the petri dish by using the command: “G1 Z1.4 F3000”
Load the Gcode file saved in step 20 of the Major step two section.
Start the bioprinting process by clicking on “Print”.
Expose the 3D HUVEC/A549 bioprinted construct to 5 min UV (2 mW/cm²) without the petri dish lid after each printing cycle.
Retrieve the 3D HUVEC/A549 construct.
Cover it with a petri dish lid.
Store the covered construct in the refrigerator for 5 minutes.
Insert DMEM-F12 media at 37°C from the side of the petri dish.
Incubate the HUVEC/A54 bioprinted constructs in an incubator for 24 hours (5% CO2, humidity of 90%, and 37°C).
Retrieve the scaffolds with a sterile spatula the next day.
Transfer the scaffolds to either a 24-well plate and add 1000 μL or to a Transwell® and add 500 μL to the bottom chamber of the well (5% CO2, humidity of 90%, and 37°C).
Change the culture medium every 2–3 days.
Prepare the bioink solution.
Transfer the solution to a 35 mm petri dish using a 1 mL pipette.
Ensure the solution is transparent and free of bubbles.
Allow the solution to cool at room temperature for 30 minutes for gelification.
Expose the sample to UV light for 5 minutes without the lid.
Remove the photocured sample with a spatula.
Stamp the samples with a puncture (Ø = ∼ 8 mm).
Hold the sample in hand.
Measure 3 points for diameter and height using a Digital Pachymeter.
Calculate the average to insert into the mechanical test machine software.
Insert the sample between the plates and test it on 1 mm/min compression mode.
Set zero compression force, touch the sample with the plate.
Apply a Preload force of 10 mN.
Proceed with the test until 90% of the cell load or the sample fracture.
Test at least five samples for each composition.
Retrieve HUVEC/A549 construct samples.
Transfer samples to a confocal dish with a spatula.
Wash the sample once with PBS at room temperature.
Dilute the Live/Dead reagent at a 1:10 ratio with media.
Add 100 μL of the diluted Live/Dead solution to the sample.
Incubate the sample at 37°C for 10 minutes.
Protect samples from light until analysis.
Seal samples with parafilm to avoid drying.
Analyze samples using a confocal microscope with 488 nm (green) and 594 nm (red) lasers.
Determine cell viability by splitting the image into green (alive) and red (dead) channels.
Calculate the area occupied by each channel.
